description: This is a baseline unsupervised neuroscience spike sorting algorithm for multi-channel extracellular recordings. This pipeline uses threshold-based event detection, waveform extraction via local maxima, channel whitening (pre-whitening), PCA-based dimensionality reduction, and clustering using HDBSCAN to automatically infer the number of units. Each detected event is reduced to a contiguous snippet around its peak, projected to PCA space, and clustered. Each event is labeled with the corresponding cluster (unit) assignment and its sample index. No ground-truth labels, simulated templates, or unit counts are used. The process is fully unsupervised, deterministic (fixed random seeds), and based strictly on provided voltage data. No units are artificially created or aligned to hidden ground-truth counts. The main steps are: (1) detect candidate spikes using a global (multi-channel) threshold; (2) extract windowed multi-channel snippets around peaks; (3) pre-whiten snippets; (4) reduce dimensionality by PCA (using a fixed number of components); (5) cluster PCA-projected snippets using HDBSCAN; (6) output spike sample indices and integer cluster/unit IDs, sorted by time, then unit ID. Event duplicate suppression enforces min refractory. Multiple parameters can be tuned for detection and snippet size, but defaults are chosen for general recordings. The output is a NumPy array (n_events, 2), with sample index and unit ID. No extra output or file/network use.
